key_insight: Quantum-state convertibility can be classified by conserved operators (and rank constraints) extracted from covariance data, yielding a much finer orbit-based taxonomy than standard symmetry-only views.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled tool for identifying state families, invariants, and exact parent Hamiltonians in quantum simulation and quantum control workflows.
method: Extract conserved operators from the kernel of a quantum covariance matrix.
Use their algebraic structure and eigenvalues to bound orbit dimension and state convertibility.
Add positive zero-eigenvalue COs to capture rank and reduced-density-matrix constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exhaustive SLOCC classifications that resolve 29 types for 4 qubits, 287 fixed types plus 4 continuous families for 5 qubits, and 4926 fixed types plus 147 continuous families for 6 qubits.
watch_item: The framework is powerful but classification grows rapidly with system size, so practical use may face computational and interpretability limits for larger multipartite systems.
paper_title: Classification of quantum states through conserved operators
